post.summary: Create a schedule-change request without changing the fixture
post.description: The proposal stores its UTC responseDeadline anchored to API createdAt plus the stage's rescheduleProposalExpiryHours (integer 1–72, default 12). It differs from minimum notice. An escalated request remains active and blocks incompatible requests. Create, counter and accept revalidate the stage's current minimum notice against the current and proposed times of every affected slot, including organizer consent. The exact boundary is inclusive; current times at or before now are exempt. Zero disables notice only: proposed dates must still be strictly future. A violation is 409 `scheduling.reschedule_notice_not_met`, with `details.anchor` equal to `current` or `proposed` (current takes priority). No request, consent, schedule or quota changes persist on denial. Recorded replays do not revalidate notice. The response carries empty capabilities; read the list for them.

get.summary: List authorized schedule-change requests for an encounter, including closed history
get.description: Computed for the authenticated actor at API time. Each request lists `allowedActions` and `blockedActions` (accept, reject and counter each appear in exactly one) plus `respondAs`, the responder accept and reject must send. `resolve` is allowed only on an escalated request for an actor with encounters.reschedule.resolve. A response is blocked once API time reaches the current proposal's `responseDeadline`, even before the expiry runner escalates it. `creation` lists the Teams the actor may request for and every scope with its current start, each with a `blockedReason`. Minimum notice and version races are not predicted; the commands still return them as errors.

200.description: The request and its full history

get.summary: Read one schedule-change request with proposals, decisions, application and operator audit
get.description: Includes `allowedActions`, `respondAs` and `blockedActions` for the authenticated actor, computed as in the list. Readable by actors who can read the Encounter; anyone else gets 404 `scheduling.schedule_change_encounter_not_found`. An unknown request, or one of another Encounter, is 404 `scheduling.schedule_change_request_not_found`.

200.description: The request as the command left it, or its replay

post.summary: Consent to the current proposal; the last required consent applies the new schedule
post.description: Answers the current proposal of an open request at `expectedVersion` only while API time is strictly before its persisted UTC responseDeadline. At the deadline or later it fails with 409 scheduling.schedule_change_response_window_closed even if the expiry runner is delayed. The actor comes from service authentication; `responder` (or `teamId`) is only the capacity claimed, and the server authorizes it. Repeating `commandKey` with the same payload replays the original outcome with `replayed: true` and no new effect. Create, counter and accept revalidate the stage's current minimum notice against the current and proposed times of every affected slot, including organizer consent. The exact boundary is inclusive; current times at or before now are exempt. Zero disables notice only: proposed dates must still be strictly future. A violation is 409 `scheduling.reschedule_notice_not_met`, with `details.anchor` equal to `current` or `proposed` (current takes priority). No request, consent, schedule or quota changes persist on denial. Recorded replays do not revalidate notice. Failures carry a stable `code`: 400 `api.validation_error`, `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_request`, `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_date` (also a `timeZone` other than the competition's), `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_reason`, `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_scope`; 403 `authorization.forbidden`, `scheduling.schedule_change_self_response_forbidden`, `scheduling.schedule_change_authority_not_required`; 404 `scheduling.schedule_change_encounter_not_found`, `scheduling.schedule_change_request_not_found`; 409 `scheduling.schedule_change_version_conflict`, `scheduling.schedule_change_proposal_stale`, `scheduling.schedule_change_request_closed`, `scheduling.schedule_change_response_window_closed`, `scheduling.schedule_change_consent_already_recorded`, `scheduling.schedule_change_idempotency_conflict`, `scheduling.schedule_change_approval_not_configured`, `scheduling.rescheduling_disabled`, `scheduling.encounter_not_editable_for_schedule_change`, `scheduling.reschedule_limit_reached`, `scheduling.fixture_update_conflict`.

post.summary: Resolve an escalated request by setting a date, keeping it or recording walkover intent
post.description: Requires encounters.reschedule.resolve for the Encounter scope. Only escalated requests can be resolved. schedule_set applies the request scope atomically and consumes the opening Team's quota; minimum notice does not block it. schedule_kept and walkover_intended keep the schedule and quota. Walkover is Scheduling intent only: no OfficialResult or official statistics are created. A nonempty reason, current proposal, expectedVersion and commandKey are required; identical retries replay the original outcome. Invalid outcomes produce 400 scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_resolution. Failures carry a stable `code`: 400 `api.validation_error`, `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_request`, `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_date` (also a `timeZone` other than the competition's), `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_reason`, `scheduling.invalid_schedule_change_scope`; 403 `authorization.forbidden`, `scheduling.schedule_change_self_response_forbidden`, `scheduling.schedule_change_authority_not_required`; 404 `scheduling.schedule_change_encounter_not_found`, `scheduling.schedule_change_request_not_found`; 409 `scheduling.schedule_change_version_conflict`, `scheduling.schedule_change_proposal_stale`, `scheduling.schedule_change_request_closed`, `scheduling.schedule_change_response_window_closed`, `scheduling.schedule_change_consent_already_recorded`, `scheduling.schedule_change_idempotency_conflict`, `scheduling.schedule_change_approval_not_configured`, `scheduling.rescheduling_disabled`, `scheduling.encounter_not_editable_for_schedule_change`, `scheduling.reschedule_limit_reached`, `scheduling.fixture_update_conflict`.

post.summary: Recalculate candidates of Encounters whose schedule change was applied
post.description: Service-only Cron target authenticated with the internal bearer secret. Consumes the durable schedule change handoff, acknowledging each application after it converges, and recalculates candidate eligibility from the stored slot starts. Earlier references stay as ineligible evidence. It never applies a schedule, selects, approves or projects statistics. Retry delivers every unacknowledged application, including one whose transaction committed late.

post.summary: Recover up to 50 expired opponent confirmation windows
post.description: Service-only Cron target authenticated with the internal bearer secret. Uses the API clock and configured provisioned RESULTS_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID; accepts no actor or timestamp from callers. Silence moves the selection to organizer_review and never approves a result. Retry discovers durable pending work.

200.description: Escalated and concurrently skipped requests in the batch

post.summary: Recover expired schedule-change proposals and escalate pending requests
post.description: Service-only runner authenticated with the internal bearer secret. Uses API time and the existing provisioned SCHEDULING_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID; accepts no caller actor or timestamp. Processes durable pending work idempotently. The request remains active when escalated; silence never changes the fixture, consumes quota or approves a result.

post.summary: Resolve organizer review by approving an exact proposal or returning to selection
post.description: Requires `encounters.results.approve` on the authenticated actor and Encounter scope. Actor, role and permissions in the body grant no authority. A nonblank reason is required. Repeating `commandKey` with the same payload returns the original outcome with `replayed: true` and no duplicate projection. Resolution approves the exact `proposalId` in the current round at `expectedVersion`, with `acknowledgeIntegrityFlags: true` when blocking flags exist, or returns to selection, releasing references and requiring a new proposal and consent. Only approval creates an official result, atomically with statistics. 404 `results.proposal_not_found`; 409 `results.integrity_flags_not_acknowledged`.
